No. No `statusLine` is set in any settings file: not `~/.claude/settings.json`, not `settings.local.json`, not the project ones. Caveman doesn't add its badge on its own. It only shows if `settings.json` points at its script, and the startup hook said that isn't set up yet.

To turn it on, add this to `~/.claude/settings.json`:

```json
"statusLine": { "type": "command", "command": "bash \"/Users/grant/.claude/hooks/caveman-statusline.sh\"" }
```

Claude Code shows only one status line at a time. Ponytail wants that spot for its own badge too. Do you want me to add the caveman one, or write a small wrapper script that shows both badges?

- Ponytail: `bash "/Users/grant/.claude/plugins/cache/ponytail/ponytail/4.10.0/hooks/ponytail-statusline.sh"`

```text
#!/bin/bash
# caveman — statusline badge script for Claude Code
# Reads the caveman mode state and outputs a colored badge.
#
# Usage in ~/.claude/settings.json:
#   "statusLine": { "type": "command", "command": "bash /path/to/caveman-statusline.sh" }
#
# Plugin users: Claude will offer to set this up on first session.
# Standalone users: install.sh wires this automatically.

CFG="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"

# Claude Code sends session JSON on stdin, including session_id. We use it to
# read THIS window's mode instead of a machine-wide flag — otherwise every
# window renders whichever mode was set last.
#
# Reading stdin must never wedge the status bar, so two guards:
#   1. `[ -t 0 ]` — a real terminal (someone running this by hand) is never
#      read from at all.
#   2. `read -t 1` — a hard ceiling if stdin is an open pipe that never closes.
#      Integer only: macOS ships bash 3.2, which rejects fractional timeouts
#      ("invalid timeout specification"). In practice Claude Code writes and
#      closes, so read returns at EOF immediately and the ceiling never fires.
# `-d ''` reads to NUL, i.e. the whole payload even if it spans lines; it exits
# nonzero at EOF, which is the normal path and not an error.
SESSION_ID=""
if [ ! -t 0 ]; then
  IFS= read -r -d '' -t 1 CAVEMAN_STDIN
  SESSION_ID=$(printf '%s' "$CAVEMAN_STDIN" \
    | grep -o '"session_id"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"[^"]*"' \
    | head -1 \
    | sed -e 's/.*:[[:space:]]*"//' -e 's/"$//')
fi

# The id becomes part of a path, so whitelist its alphabet AND cap its length —
# same rule as validateSessionId in caveman-config.js and the regex in the .ps1
# port. Anything else, including empty, falls back to the legacy flag.
case "$SESSION_ID" in
  ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9_-]*) SESSION_ID="" ;;
esac
[ "${#SESSION_ID}" -gt 128 ] && SESSION_ID=""

FLAG="$CFG/.caveman-active"
if [ -n "$SESSION_ID" ] && [ -f "$CFG/.caveman-sessions/$SESSION_ID.mode" ]; then
  FLAG="$CFG/.caveman-sessions/$SESSION_ID.mode"
fi

# Refuse symlinks — a local attacker could point the flag at ~/.ssh/id_rsa and
# have the statusline render its bytes (including ANSI escape sequences) to
# the terminal every keystroke.
[ -L "$FLAG" ] && exit 0
[ ! -f "$FLAG" ] && exit 0

# Hard-cap the read at 64 bytes and strip anything outside [a-z0-9-] — blocks
# terminal-escape injection and OSC hyperlink spoofing via the flag contents.
MODE=$(head -c 64 "$FLAG" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\n\r' | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
MODE=$(printf '%s' "$MODE" | tr -cd 'a-z0-9-')

# Durable off: caveman is deactivated for this session. Render nothing at all,
# matching what an absent flag does — never "[CAVEMAN:OFF]", which would read
# as a caveman mode rather than the absence of one.
[ "$MODE" = "off" ] && exit 0

# Whitelist and badge map in one. Pre-three-skill level names (lite, full,
# ultra, wenyan*) still sit in older session files and mirrors; they render
# as the skill they became. Anything else → render nothing rather than echo
# attacker bytes.
case "$MODE" in
  caveman|lite|full) BADGE="CAVEMAN" ;;
  ultracave|ultra) BADGE="ULTRACAVE" ;;
  megacave|wenyan|wenyan-lite|wenyan-full|wenyan-ultra) BADGE="MEGACAVE" ;;
  commit|review|compress) BADGE="CAVEMAN:$(printf '%s' "$MODE" | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]')" ;;
  *) exit 0 ;;
esac

printf '\033[38;5;172m[%s]\033[0m' "$BADGE"

# Historical numeric savings suffixes are not measurements. Ignore them,
# including files written by older stats scripts before this update.
exit 0
=====PONYTAIL=====
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR overrides ~/.claude, matching where the hooks write the flag (issue #34)
flag="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/.ponytail-active"
[ -f "$flag" ] || exit 0

mode=$(head -n1 "$flag" | tr -d '[:space:]')

# ultra is the high-intensity mode; flag it amber so it stands out from the
# default green at a glance. The level is still in the text, so color is a
# redundant cue, not the only one.
color=108
[ "$mode" = "ultra" ] && color=173

if [ -z "$mode" ] || [ "$mode" = "full" ]; then
    printf '\033[38;5;%sm[PONYTAIL]\033[0m' "$color"
else
    printf '\033[38;5;%sm[PONYTAIL:%s]\033[0m' "$color" "$(printf '%s' "$mode" | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]')"
fi
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-21 00:43:39Z)**_

Each script prints a single colored badge showing the plugin's current mode, and nothing else. No model, directory, git branch, or token info.

**Caveman** (orange):
- Default: `[CAVEMAN]`
- Other modes: `[ULTRACAVE]`, `[MEGACAVE]`, or `[CAVEMAN:COMMIT]` / `:REVIEW` / `:COMPRESS`
- When caveman is off: shows nothing
- It reads the mode for the current window, so different windows can show different modes.

**Ponytail**:
- Default (`full`): `[PONYTAIL]` in green
- Other modes: `[PONYTAIL:LITE]` in green, or `[PONYTAIL:ULTRA]` in amber
- When ponytail is off: shows nothing
- It reads one shared flag file, so every window shows whatever mode was set last.

If you want them together, a wrapper could show both side by side: `[CAVEMAN] [PONYTAIL]`.

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Combined statusline: caveman + ponytail mode badges, space-separated.
CFG="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"

# Caveman needs the session JSON on stdin to pick this window's mode.
[ -t 0 ] || input=$(cat)
cave=$(printf '%s' "$input" | bash "$CFG/hooks/caveman-statusline.sh")

# Ponytail's script lives under a versioned cache dir; use the newest.
pony_script=$(ls -d "$CFG"/plugins/cache/ponytail/ponytail/*/hooks/ponytail-statusline.sh 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1)
[ -n "$pony_script" ] && pony=$(bash "$pony_script")

printf '%s' "$cave${cave:+${pony:+ }}$pony"

```

```text
-rw-r--r--@ 1 grant  staff  2346 Jun 11 22:11 /Users/grant/.claude/statusline-command.sh
#!/usr/bin/env sh
# Claude Code status line — styled after Powerlevel10k lean prompt (p10k)
# Left:  dir  branch-icon git-branch [git-flags]
# Right: model  context%

# Ensure Homebrew tools (jq, git) resolve even under a minimal PATH
export PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:$PATH"

input=$(cat)

current_dir=$(echo "$input" | jq -r '.workspace.current_dir // .cwd')
model=$(echo "$input" | jq -r '.model.display_name')
used_pct=$(echo "$input" | jq -r '.context_window.used_percentage // empty')

# Directory: full path, home-relative (e.g. ~/code/project or ~)
home_dir="$HOME"
case "$current_dir" in
  "$home_dir") dir="~" ;;
  "$home_dir"/*) dir="~${current_dir#$home_dir}" ;;
  *) dir="$current_dir" ;;
esac

# Git branch + status flags (--no-optional-locks avoids stale lock issues)
git_branch=$(git -C "$current_dir" --no-optional-locks branch --show-current 2>/dev/null || true)
git_part=""
if [ -n "$git_branch" ]; then
  git_flags=""
  # Staged changes (+)
  staged=$(git -C "$current_dir" --no-optional-locks diff --cached --name-only 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
  [ "$staged" -gt 0 ] && git_flags="${git_flags}+"
  # Unstaged changes (!)
  unstaged=$(git -C "$current_dir" --no-optional-locks diff --name-only 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
  [ "$unstaged" -gt 0 ] && git_flags="${git_flags}!"
  # Untracked files (?)
  untracked=$(git -C "$current_dir" --no-optional-locks ls-files --others --exclude-standard 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
  [ "$untracked" -gt 0 ] && git_flags="${git_flags}?"
  # Ahead/behind remote
  ahead=$(git -C "$current_dir" --no-optional-locks rev-list --count @{u}..HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  behind=$(git -C "$current_dir" --no-optional-locks rev-list --count HEAD..@{u} 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  [ "$behind" -gt 0 ] && git_flags="${git_flags}⇣${behind}"
  [ "$ahead"  -gt 0 ] && git_flags="${git_flags}⇡${ahead}"

  # p10k uses  (git branch icon) before the branch name
  if [ -n "$git_flags" ]; then
    git_part="  ${git_branch} ${git_flags}"
  else
    git_part="  ${git_branch}"
  fi
fi

# Context window usage
ctx_part=""
if [ -n "$used_pct" ]; then
  used_int=$(printf "%.0f" "$used_pct")
  ctx_part=" · ctx ${used_int}%"
fi

# Assemble: left (dir + git) separated from right (model + ctx) by a centre dot
printf "%s%s · %s%s\n" "$dir" "$git_part" "$model" "$ctx_part"
```

what is the default claude code statusline

---

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-21 00:47:38Z)**_

There isn't one. When `statusLine` isn't set, Claude Code leaves that spot empty, which is why nothing showed after you turned yours off. Its built-in footer (for example, the permission mode indicator) appears either way and isn't the status line.

The status line is opt-in. You either point `statusLine` at a command, as we just did, or run `/statusline` and Claude Code writes one for you.

```text
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');
const os = require('os');
const { getClaudeDir, getConfigDir } = require('./ponytail-config');

const STATE_FILE = '.ponytail-active';

// ponytail: VS Code Copilot never sets COPILOT_PLUGIN_DATA — it only injects
// CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, pointed at an install path under .vscode/agent-plugins/
// (#528). Without this fallback isCopilot was false, so ponytail assumed
// native Claude Code and emitted the statusline nudge, which VS Code Copilot
// doesn't read.
function isVsCodeCopilotRoot(pluginRoot) {
  if (!pluginRoot) return false;
  return pluginRoot.split(/[\\/]+/).includes('agent-plugins') &&
    pluginRoot.toLowerCase().includes('.vscode');
}

const isCopilot = Boolean(process.env.COPILOT_PLUGIN_DATA) ||
  isVsCodeCopilotRoot(process.env.CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT);
const isCodex = !isCopilot && Boolean(process.env.PLUGIN_DATA);
const isQoder = !isCopilot && !isCodex && Boolean(process.env.QODER_SESSION_ID);
// Cursor (#817): CURSOR_VERSION is set only in the environment Cursor builds
// for hook processes (Cursor 3.20.17 assigns it in exactly one place, the hook
// env builder), so it never leaks into a Claude Code session running inside
// Cursor's terminal. Cursor also sets it when it runs a Claude-format plugin's
// hooks next to CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, and it needs Cursor-shaped JSON either
// way, so this check comes after the hosts with their own data dirs.
const isCursor = !isCopilot && !isCodex && !isQoder && Boolean(process.env.CURSOR_VERSION);

let stateDir = getClaudeDir();
if (isCodex) stateDir = process.env.PLUGIN_DATA;
// COPILOT_PLUGIN_DATA is unset under VS Code Copilot, so fall back to
// getClaudeDir() rather than building a path from undefined.
if (isCopilot) stateDir = process.env.COPILOT_PLUGIN_DATA || getClaudeDir();
if (isQoder) stateDir = path.join(os.homedir(), '.qoder');
if (isCursor) stateDir = path.join(os.homedir(), '.cursor');

const statePath = path.join(stateDir, STATE_FILE);

function setMode(mode) {
  fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(statePath), { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(statePath, mode);
}

function clearMode() {
  try { fs.unlinkSync(statePath); } catch (e) {}
}

// Live mode written by activate/mode-tracker. Absent flag = ponytail off.
function readMode() {
  try {
    return fs.readFileSync(statePath, 'utf8').trim() || null;
  } catch (e) {
    return null;
  }
}

// Cursor's always-on project rule (.cursor/rules/ponytail.mdc) already puts the
// ruleset in front of every prompt and no hook can switch a rule off, so while
// it is in the workspace the hooks step back instead of injecting a second,
// possibly contradicting, copy (#817). Cursor hands every hook the workspace
// root as CURSOR_PROJECT_DIR; project hooks also run from that directory.
// ponytail: first workspace root only, a rule in a secondary folder of a
// multi-root workspace goes undetected.
function cursorRulePath() {
  const root = process.env.CURSOR_PROJECT_DIR || process.cwd();
  const rule = path.join(root, '.cursor', 'rules', 'ponytail.mdc');
  return fs.existsSync(rule) ? rule : null;
}

function cursorRuleNotice(rule) {
  return 'PONYTAIL: the always-on Cursor rule ' + rule + ' is active in this workspace and ' +
    'already carries the ponytail ruleset, so the ponytail hooks injected nothing further. ' +
    'Mode switching (/ponytail lite|full|ultra|off, "stop ponytail") is unavailable while ' +
    'that rule exists. When the user tries to switch or turn off ponytail, tell them to ' +
    'delete that rule so hooks.json can manage the level.';
}
```

```text
// plus the one-shot modes and the durable off.
const VALID_MODES = [
  'off', 'caveman', 'ultracave', 'megacave',
  'commit', 'review', 'compress'
];

// Startup policy only: manual starts inactive, but explicit activation uses
// caveman. Keep it out of flag validation and the selectable modes.
const VALID_DEFAULT_MODES = [...VALID_MODES, 'manual'];

// The six intensity levels that preceded the three skills. Session files,
// .caveman-active mirrors, config files, env vars and mode-log rows written
// before the switch still hold these, so every read maps them forward and no
// write ever emits one.
const LEGACY_MODES = {
  lite: 'caveman', full: 'caveman', ultra: 'ultracave',
  wenyan: 'megacave', 'wenyan-lite': 'megacave',
  'wenyan-full': 'megacave', 'wenyan-ultra': 'megacave',
};

// Stored/configured value → current mode id, or null when it is neither a
// mode nor a legacy level. The whitelist every read path goes through.
function canonicalMode(raw) {
  if (typeof raw !== 'string') return null;
  const m = raw.toLowerCase();
  if (VALID_MODES.includes(m)) return m;
  return Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(LEGACY_MODES, m) ? LEGACY_MODES[m] : null;
}
```

<summary>Tool use: **Write**</summary>

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Combined statusline: p10k-style line, then right-aligned caveman + ponytail
# mode badges. Badges never hide, so a broken plugin is visible:
#   OFF = turned off, or plugin disabled in settings.json
#   ?   = no state written for this session (activation hook didn't run)
#   ERR = state file is a symlink or holds an unknown mode
CFG="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"
export PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:$PATH"
export LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8 # so ${#var} counts characters, not bytes

[ -t 0 ] || input=$(cat)
base=$(printf '%s' "$input" | sh "$CFG/statusline-command.sh")

enabled() { jq -e --arg p "$1" '.enabledPlugins[$p] == true' "$CFG/settings.json" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
upper() { printf '%s' "$1" | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]'; }

# Prints the flag's mode, "" if missing, "!" if a symlink. Capped and stripped
# to [a-z0-9-] so flag contents can't inject terminal escapes.
read_flag() {
  if [ -L "$1" ]; then echo '!'; return; fi
  [ -f "$1" ] && head -c 64 "$1" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | tr -cd 'a-z0-9-'
}

# Caveman tracks mode per session; its SessionStart hook always writes the
# file (even for "off"), so a missing one means the hook didn't run.
sid=$(printf '%s' "$input" | jq -r '.session_id // empty' 2>/dev/null)
case "$sid" in *[!A-Za-z0-9_-]*) sid="" ;; esac
cflag="$CFG/.caveman-active"
[ -n "$sid" ] && cflag="$CFG/.caveman-sessions/$sid.mode"

if ! enabled caveman@caveman; then
  cave="CAVE:OFF"
else
  m=$(read_flag "$cflag")
  case "$m" in
    caveman | lite | full) cave="CAVE" ;;
    ultracave | ultra) cave="CAVE:ULTRA" ;;
    megacave | wenyan*) cave="CAVE:MEGA" ;;
    commit | review | compress) cave="CAVE:$(upper "$m")" ;;
    off) cave="CAVE:OFF" ;;
    "") cave="CAVE:?" ;;
    *) cave="CAVE:ERR" ;;
  esac
fi

# Ponytail keeps one global flag and deletes it on "stop ponytail", so a
# missing flag reads as off.
if ! enabled ponytail@ponytail; then
  pony="PONY:OFF"
else
  m=$(read_flag "$CFG/.ponytail-active")
  case "$m" in
    full) pony="PONY" ;;
    lite | ultra) pony="PONY:$(upper "$m")" ;;
    "" | off) pony="PONY:OFF" ;;
    *) pony="PONY:ERR" ;;
  esac
fi

color() {
  case "$1" in
    *:OFF) echo 244 ;;
    *:\? | *:ERR) echo 167 ;;
    PONY:ULTRA) echo 173 ;;
    PONY*) echo 108 ;;
    *) echo 172 ;;
  esac
}

# Claude Code indents the statusline; raise margin if the badges wrap.
margin=4
plain="[$cave] [$pony]"
pad=$((${COLUMNS:-0} - margin - ${#base} - ${#plain}))
[ "$pad" -lt 1 ] && pad=1

printf '%s%*s' "$base" "$pad" ''
printf '\033[38;5;%sm[%s]\033[0m \033[38;5;%sm[%s]\033[0m' "$(color "$cave")" "$cave" "$(color "$pony")" "$pony"

```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-21 00:53:41Z)**_

All three changes are in `~/.claude/hooks/statusline.sh`. I tested them in the shell. I can't see the real status bar, so check that the right alignment looks right on your screen.

With this session's info at 122 columns:
```
~/code/nasa-picture-proxy  dev !?⇡9 · Opus 5.5 · ctx 10%                       [CAVE] [PONY]
```

**Short names, suffixes kept:**
- Caveman: `CAVE`, `CAVE:ULTRA`, `CAVE:MEGA`, `CAVE:COMMIT`, `CAVE:REVIEW`, `CAVE:COMPRESS`
- Ponytail: `PONY`, `PONY:LITE`, `PONY:ULTRA`
- Colors are the same as before.

**Off or broken badges now stay visible:**

| Badge | Color | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `:OFF` | gray | Turned off, or plugin disabled in `settings.json` |
| `:?` | red | Caveman never wrote a mode for this session, so its startup hook didn't run (for example, `node` isn't on the PATH the hooks use) |
| `:ERR` | red | Mode file is a symlink or holds a mode the script doesn't recognize |

I tested all of these states against a throwaway config folder, and each one showed the right badge.

**Right alignment:** Claude Code passes the terminal width (`COLUMNS`) to the status line script, so the badges are pushed to the right edge, with 4 columns kept free. If they wrap or sit too far left, change `margin=4` in the script. In a narrow terminal they fall back to a single space after the path line.

**Limits:**
- Ponytail deletes its mode file when you stop it. So if its startup hook fails, it shows `PONY:OFF` rather than `?`, because the two cases look the same.
- The enabled check only reads `~/.claude/settings.json`. A plugin turned on or off in a project's settings isn't detected.

While checking the screen width, I saved a debug dump to the scratchpad. It captured an environment token in plain text. I hid the token from the output and deleted the file.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-21 01:09:21Z)**_

Yes, it makes sense here, mostly because of your earlier point about plugins being fiddly. If each section runs as its own small script, one broken section can't take down the whole line. The main script can show a red `[caveman!]` instead, so you see what broke.

Proposed layout:

```
~/.claude/statusline-command.sh   # entry point: reads session JSON, runs modules, aligns
~/.claude/statusline/
  dir.sh  git.sh  model.sh  context.sh  caveman.sh  ponytail.sh
```

The section order lives in two lines at the top of the entry point:

```bash
LEFT="dir git"
RIGHT="model context caveman ponytail"
```

- **To disable a section:** delete its name from the list. To reorder, move the name.
- **To add a section:** drop a new script in `statusline/` and add its name to a list.
- **How a section works:** each script receives the session info and prints its piece of the line, or prints nothing to hide itself. The entry point handles spacing, separators and right alignment, so section scripts stay small.
- **If a section fails:** a missing script or one that exits with an error shows as a red `[name!]` instead of disappearing.

The cost is about six extra small processes each time the line refreshes. That adds a few milliseconds, which you won't notice.

Should I build this? It would replace `hooks/statusline.sh` and split your current script into the modules above, and the line would look exactly as it does now. I'd leave caveman's own `hooks/caveman-statusline.sh` alone, since the plugin installed it.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-21 01:11:10Z)**_

I checked it, and the separate-folder version is over-engineered for a status line this size. That reverses what I suggested last time.

**What the folder version would cost:**
- **Shared code gets split.** The caveman and ponytail badges use the same helpers and the same colors. Separate files mean either copying that code into each one, so a color change needs two edits, or adding a shared helper file, which is one more piece to keep track of.
- **More rules.** Every section script would need to follow the same input/output conventions.
- **More processes.** About six extra small processes on every refresh.
- **The failure isolation I pitched is weak.** A runtime error in one part of a bash script doesn't stop the rest of the script. The failures you actually worry about are plugin state problems, and the `OFF`/`?`/`ERR` badges already cover those. A typo is the one thing that would break a single file, and you'd notice that right away because you just made the edit.

**What you actually want** is to turn sections on and off and edit them separately. One file gives you both:

```bash
LEFT="dir git"
RIGHT="model caveman ponytail"

section_dir()      { ... }
section_git()      { ... }
section_model()    { ... }   # model + context together
section_caveman()  { ... }
section_ponytail() { ... }
```

- You toggle or reorder by editing those two lines, and edit a section by changing its function.
- The helpers and colors exist once.
- A name in the list with no matching function shows a red `[name!]`. That check is one line.
- Model and context stay one section. If they were split and you turned off model, the context text would start with a stray `·`.

A `~/.claude/statusline/` folder starts to make sense if sections grow large or you want to drop in other people's sections. Until then it's extra structure for about 100 lines of script.

Should I build the single-file version in `~/.claude/statusline-command.sh`, point `settings.json` back at it, and delete `hooks/statusline.sh`?

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="Write"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Write**</summary>

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Claude Code status line — styled after Powerlevel10k lean prompt (p10k),
# plus caveman + ponytail mode badges.
#
# Toggle or reorder sections by editing these lists. Each name maps to a
# section_<name> function below that prints its text, or nothing to hide.
# LEFT renders at the start of the line, RIGHT is right-aligned.
LEFT="dir git"
RIGHT="model caveman ponytail"

# Ensure Homebrew tools (jq, git) resolve even under a minimal PATH
export PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:$PATH"
export LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8 # so ${#var} counts characters, not bytes
CFG="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"

[ -t 0 ] || input=$(cat)
field() { printf '%s' "$input" | jq -r "$1 // empty" 2>/dev/null; }
current_dir=$(field '.workspace.current_dir // .cwd')

# Directory: full path, home-relative (e.g. ~/code/project or ~)
section_dir() {
  case "$current_dir" in
    "$HOME") echo "~" ;;
    "$HOME"/*) echo "~${current_dir#$HOME}" ;;
    *) echo "$current_dir" ;;
  esac
}

# Git branch + status flags (--no-optional-locks avoids stale lock issues)
g() { git -C "$current_dir" --no-optional-locks "$@" 2>/dev/null; }
section_git() {
  branch=$(g branch --show-current)
  [ -n "$branch" ] || return
  flags=""
  [ -n "$(g diff --cached --name-only)" ] && flags="${flags}+"                # staged
  [ -n "$(g diff --name-only)" ] && flags="${flags}!"                         # unstaged
  [ -n "$(g ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ] && flags="${flags}?"     # untracked
  behind=$(g rev-list --count HEAD..@{u} || echo 0)
  ahead=$(g rev-list --count @{u}..HEAD || echo 0)
  [ "$behind" -gt 0 ] && flags="${flags}⇣${behind}"
  [ "$ahead" -gt 0 ] && flags="${flags}⇡${ahead}"
  echo "$branch${flags:+ $flags}"
}

# Model name + context window usage
section_model() {
  pct=$(field '.context_window.used_percentage')
  [ -n "$pct" ] && pct=" · ctx $(printf '%.0f' "$pct")%"
  echo "$(field '.model.display_name')$pct"
}

# Plugin mode badges never hide, so a broken plugin is visible:
#   OFF = turned off, or plugin disabled in settings.json
#   ?   = no state written for this session (activation hook didn't run)
#   ERR = state file is a symlink or holds an unknown mode
# Green = normal mode, amber = stronger mode, gray = off, red = broken.
badge() {
  case "$1" in
    *:OFF) c=244 ;;
    *:\? | *:ERR | *!) c=167 ;;
    *:ULTRA | *:MEGA) c=173 ;;
    *) c=108 ;;
  esac
  printf '\033[38;5;%sm[%s]\033[0m' "$c" "$1"
}
enabled() { jq -e --arg p "$1" '.enabledPlugins[$p] == true' "$CFG/settings.json" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
upper() { printf '%s' "$1" | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]'; }

# Prints the flag's mode, "" if missing, "!" if a symlink. Capped and stripped
# to [a-z0-9-] so flag contents can't inject terminal escapes.
read_flag() {
  if [ -L "$1" ]; then echo '!'; return; fi
  [ -f "$1" ] && head -c 64 "$1" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | tr -cd 'a-z0-9-'
}

# Caveman tracks mode per session; its SessionStart hook always writes the
# file (even for "off"), so a missing one means the hook didn't run.
section_caveman() {
  enabled caveman@caveman || { badge "CAVE:OFF"; return; }
  sid=$(field '.session_id')
  case "$sid" in *[!A-Za-z0-9_-]*) sid="" ;; esac
  flag="$CFG/.caveman-active"
  [ -n "$sid" ] && flag="$CFG/.caveman-sessions/$sid.mode"
  m=$(read_flag "$flag")
  case "$m" in
    caveman | lite | full) badge "CAVE" ;;
    ultracave | ultra) badge "CAVE:ULTRA" ;;
    megacave | wenyan*) badge "CAVE:MEGA" ;;
    commit | review | compress) badge "CAVE:$(upper "$m")" ;;
    off) badge "CAVE:OFF" ;;
    "") badge "CAVE:?" ;;
    *) badge "CAVE:ERR" ;;
  esac
}

# Ponytail keeps one global flag and deletes it on "stop ponytail", so a
# missing flag reads as off.
section_ponytail() {
  enabled ponytail@ponytail || { badge "PONY:OFF"; return; }
  m=$(read_flag "$CFG/.ponytail-active")
  case "$m" in
    full) badge "PONY" ;;
    lite | ultra) badge "PONY:$(upper "$m")" ;;
    "" | off) badge "PONY:OFF" ;;
    *) badge "PONY:ERR" ;;
  esac
}

# Runs each named section and joins the non-empty results with $1. A name with
# no section_<name> function renders as a red [name!].
render() {
  sep=$1 out=""
  shift
  for s in "$@"; do
    if declare -F "section_$s" >/dev/null; then text=$("section_$s"); else text=$(badge "$s!"); fi
    [ -n "$text" ] && out="${out:+$out$sep}$text"
  done
  printf '%s' "$out"
}

left=$(render "  " $LEFT)
right=$(render " " $RIGHT)

# Claude Code indents the statusline; raise margin if the right side wraps.
margin=4
visible() { printf '%s' "$1" | sed $'s/\e\\[[0-9;]*m//g'; }
plain_left=$(visible "$left")
plain_right=$(visible "$right")
pad=$((${COLUMNS:-0} - margin - ${#plain_left} - ${#plain_right}))
[ "$pad" -lt 1 ] && pad=1

printf '%s%*s%s' "$left" "$pad" '' "$right"

```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-21 01:19:00Z)**_

Claude Code already sends plenty of data to the status line on every refresh, so each of these would be a small section. Ranked by how useful I think they are:

1. **Rate limits.** Your 5-hour and 7-day usage, plus when each resets, e.g. `5h 1% · 7d 0%`. It could stay hidden until usage passes a threshold such as 50%. This is the one most likely to save you from hitting a limit unexpectedly.
2. **Effort level.** Shows `xhigh` or `high`, so you can see that `/effort` took effect. Fast mode could appear here as `⚡` when it's on.
3. **Lines changed.** Shows `+24 −3` for this session. That's a quick check on how much Claude has edited.
4. **Session cost.** Shows `$1.18`. It's less meaningful on a subscription, but you'd notice a runaway session.
5. **Prompt cache.** Shows a warning only when the cache has gone cold or expires soon. I'd skip this one, because Claude Code manages the cache itself.

I'd skip session duration, the Claude Code version and the output style. You'd rarely look at them, and they'd crowd the line.

My pick would be 1 and 2 on the right side, before the badges. Which of these do you want?

```text
//
// `.caveman-sessions` is the ownership marker: both statusline scripts read the
// session store, and verify_repo.py pins that string in each of them. A file at
// the stable path without it is the user's own script and is never touched.
const STATUSLINE_MARKER = (cfg.SESSIONS_DIRNAME || '.caveman-sessions');

// The stable copy to recommend, or null to keep the caller on __dirname. Copies
// only when the destination is absent or is a caveman script that has drifted
// from the running one — so a plugin update reaches the badge, and a foreign or
// hand-edited script survives untouched.
function stableStatuslinePath(scriptName) {
  try {
    const source = path.join(__dirname, scriptName);
    const target = path.join(claudeDir, 'hooks', scriptName);
    if (path.resolve(source) === path.resolve(target)) return target; // standalone install
    const wanted = fs.readFileSync(source, 'utf8');
    if (!wanted.includes(STATUSLINE_MARKER)) return null; // not a script we recognize
    if (fs.existsSync(target)) {
      const current = fs.readFileSync(target, 'utf8');
      if (current === wanted) return target;
      if (!current.includes(STATUSLINE_MARKER)) return null; // foreign — leave it alone
    return false; // missing on either side, or unreadable: not provably outdated
  }
}

try {
  const isWindows = process.platform === 'win32';
  const scriptName = isWindows ? 'caveman-statusline.ps1' : 'caveman-statusline.sh';

  let hasStatusline = false;
  let staleCommand = null;
  let staleKind = null; // 'gone' | 'outdated'
  if (fs.existsSync(settingsPath)) {
    let configured;
    try {
      configured = parseSettingsFile(settingsPath).statusLine;
      hasStatusline = !!configured;
    } catch (e) {
      // Unparseable even as JSONC. Fall back to a substring probe and err
      // toward NOT nudging: a spurious "set up your statusline" for a user who
      // already has one is worse than a missing nudge. The command cannot be
      // extracted on this path, so a stale one is not detected either.
      hasStatusline = fs.readFileSync(settingsPath, 'utf8').includes('"statusLine"');
    }
    const scripts = hasStatusline && configured ? statuslineScripts(configured.command) : null;
    if (scripts) {
      // An accepted stable copy (<claudeDir>/hooks/) is ours to keep current:
      // refresh it from the running script, not only when nudging.
      for (const script of scripts) {
        const name = path.basename(script);
        if (path.resolve(script) === path.resolve(claudeDir, 'hooks', name)) stableStatuslinePath(name);
      }
```

```text
      local branch=${(V)VCS_STATUS_LOCAL_BRANCH}
      # If local branch name is at most 32 characters long, show it in full.
      # Otherwise show the first 12 … the last 12.
      # Tip: To always show local branch name in full without truncation, delete the next line.
      (( $#branch > 32 )) && branch[13,-13]="…"  # <-- this line
      res+="${clean}${(g::)POWERLEVEL9K_VCS_BRANCH_ICON}${branch//\%/%%}"
    fi

    if [[ -n $VCS_STATUS_TAG
          # Show tag only if not on a branch.
          # Tip: To always show tag, delete the next line.
          && -z $VCS_STATUS_LOCAL_BRANCH  # <-- this line
        ]]; then
      local tag=${(V)VCS_STATUS_TAG}
      # If tag name is at most 32 characters long, show it in full.
      # Otherwise show the first 12 … the last 12.
      # Tip: To always show tag name in full without truncation, delete the next line.
      (( $#tag > 32 )) && tag[13,-13]="…"  # <-- this line
      res+="${meta}#${clean}${tag//\%/%%}"
    fi

    # Display the current Git commit if there is no branch and no tag.
    # Tip: To always display the current Git commit, delete the next line.
    [[ -z $VCS_STATUS_LOCAL_BRANCH && -z $VCS_STATUS_TAG ]] &&  # <-- this line
      res+="${meta}@${clean}${VCS_STATUS_COMMIT[1,8]}"

    # Show tracking branch name if it differs from local branch.
    if [[ -n ${VCS_STATUS_REMOTE_BRANCH:#$VCS_STATUS_LOCAL_BRANCH} ]]; then
      res+="${meta}:${clean}${(V)VCS_STATUS_REMOTE_BRANCH//\%/%%}"
    fi

    # Display "wip" if the latest commit's summary contains "wip" or "WIP".
    if [[ $VCS_STATUS_COMMIT_SUMMARY == (|*[^[:alnum:]])(wip|WIP)(|[^[:alnum:]]*) ]]; then
      res+=" ${modified}wip"
    fi

    if (( VCS_STATUS_COMMITS_AHEAD || VCS_STATUS_COMMITS_BEHIND )); then
      # ⇣42 if behind the remote.
      (( VCS_STATUS_COMMITS_BEHIND )) && res+=" ${clean}⇣${VCS_STATUS_COMMITS_BEHIND}"
      # ⇡42 if ahead of the remote; no leading space if also behind the remote: ⇣42⇡42.
      (( VCS_STATUS_COMMITS_AHEAD && !VCS_STATUS_COMMITS_BEHIND )) && res+=" "
      (( VCS_STATUS_COMMITS_AHEAD  )) && res+="${clean}⇡${VCS_STATUS_COMMITS_AHEAD}"
    elif [[ -n $VCS_STATUS_REMOTE_BRANCH ]]; then
      # Tip: Uncomment the next line to display '=' if up to date with the remote.
      # res+=" ${clean}="
    fi

    # ⇠42 if behind the push remote.
    (( VCS_STATUS_PUSH_COMMITS_BEHIND )) && res+=" ${clean}⇠${VCS_STATUS_PUSH_COMMITS_BEHIND}"
    (( VCS_STATUS_PUSH_COMMITS_AHEAD && !VCS_STATUS_PUSH_COMMITS_BEHIND )) && res+=" "
    # ⇢42 if ahead of the push remote; no leading space if also behind: ⇠42⇢42.
    (( VCS_STATUS_PUSH_COMMITS_AHEAD  )) && res+="${clean}⇢${VCS_STATUS_PUSH_COMMITS_AHEAD}"
    # *42 if have stashes.
    (( VCS_STATUS_STASHES        )) && res+=" ${clean}*${VCS_STATUS_STASHES}"
    # 'merge' if the repo is in an unusual state.
    [[ -n $VCS_STATUS_ACTION     ]] && res+=" ${conflicted}${VCS_STATUS_ACTION}"
    # ~42 if have merge conflicts.
    (( VCS_STATUS_NUM_CONFLICTED )) && res+=" ${conflicted}~${VCS_STATUS_NUM_CONFLICTED}"
    # +42 if have staged changes.
    (( VCS_STATUS_NUM_STAGED     )) && res+=" ${modified}+${VCS_STATUS_NUM_STAGED}"
    # !42 if have unstaged changes.
    (( VCS_STATUS_NUM_UNSTAGED   )) && res+=" ${modified}!${VCS_STATUS_NUM_UNSTAGED}"
    # ?42 if have untracked files. It's really a question mark, your font isn't broken.
    # See POWERLEVEL9K_VCS_UNTRACKED_ICON above if you want to use a different icon.
    # Remove the next line if you don't want to see untracked files at all.
    (( VCS_STATUS_NUM_UNTRACKED  )) && res+=" ${untracked}${(g::)POWERLEVEL9K_VCS_UNTRACKED_ICON}${VCS_STATUS_NUM_UNTRACKED}"
    # "─" if the number of unstaged files is unknown. This can happen due to
    # POWERLEVEL9K_VCS_MAX_INDEX_SIZE_DIRTY (see below) being set to a non-negative number lower
    # than the number of files in the Git index, or due to bash.showDirtyState being set to false
    # in the repository config. The number of staged and untracked files may also be unknown
    # in this case.
    (( VCS_STATUS_HAS_UNSTAGED == -1 )) && res+=" ${modified}─"

    typeset -g my_git_format=$res
  }
  functions -M my_git_formatter 2>/dev/null
```

Yes. The status line now uses your p10k icons and colors. In a shell test it printed:

```
 ~/code/nasa-picture-proxy    dev ⇡9 *2 !2 ?13  +24 −3        Opus 5.5 high · ctx 10% [CAVE][PONY]
```

The icons show as blanks here because my output isn't in a Nerd Font. Your terminal should render them, but I can't see the real status bar, so check it.

**What now matches your prompt:**
- **Icons:** a folder icon before the path, then the GitHub cat and branch icon. I checked the codepoints against your installed p10k files. Repos not on GitHub get the plain git icon. Your home folder and folders outside it get the matching p10k folder icons.
- **Path colors:** blue `31` for the path, with the last folder in bold `39`, taken from `~/.p10k.zsh`.
- **Git colors and counts:** taken from your `my_git_formatter`. Branch, ⇣/⇡ and stashes (`*`) are green `76`, staged (`+`) and unstaged (`!`) are yellow `178`, untracked (`?`) is blue `39`, and conflicts (`~`) are red `196`. The flags now show counts like `!2 ?13` rather than bare `!?`.
- **Stashes and conflicts** are new. A detached HEAD shows `@<commit>` like p10k does, where the old script showed nothing.

Git status now comes from one git command instead of six, so each refresh is cheaper.

I hit one bug along the way and fixed it. The bash that ships with macOS (3.2) swallowed the first byte of the `⇡` arrow when it came right after a color variable, which broke the text. Wrapping the variable in braces (`${green}⇡`) fixed it, and the output is now valid UTF-8 at the expected width.

Your prompt screenshot shows `?9`, while git currently reports 13 untracked files here, with or without collapsed folders. The screenshot was probably taken at a different moment.
